Join Duke's Department of Religious Studies and Duke Libraries with author Michael Blanding, author of The Gospel According to Hobby Lobby: Inside a Billionaire Family's Quest to Craft a Christian Nation, as we explore his book and the Hobby Lobby antiquities scandal. Blanding will discuss the Green family's acquisition of thousands of looted, stolen, and forged biblical artifacts for the Museum of the Bible in Washington, D.C. Drawing on previously unseen documents, interviews, and original reporting, he will share insights into the investigation, the international antiquities trade, and the legal and ethical questions surrounding the acquisition and collection of cultural heritage objects.

item.title: Cello Studios of Caroline Stinson and Stephanie Vial: Feeling American — Tue Nov 17, 7:30 PM — East Duke 201 - Nelson Music Room
item.description:
Music makes us feel-alive, emotional, and deeply human. But what makes music distinctly American?
In this studio recital, Duke cellists explore works by American composers and others who sought to capture the sound, spirit, and experience of America. Through a wide-ranging program, the performers consider how music can reflect identity, place, memory, and the many evolving ideas of what it means to be American.
This performance is part of "We the People," a Duke and Durham collaboration marking the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence through public events that examine the nation's evolving identity. Drawing from the opening words of the Constitution, the project invites us to consider who "the people" have been and who we aspire to be within the ongoing story of the United States.
This event is free and open to the public. All are welcome.
Source: Duke Arts, Duke University

item.title: Joint Invasive Removal with Wake Audubon (Fuquay-Varina) — Wed Nov 18, 9:00 AM
item.description:
NCWF South Wake Conservationists Chapter is partners with Wake Audubon’s ongoing project to conserve and support the natural heritage of a unique nature park in Fuquay-Varina, the Carroll Howard Johnson Environmental Education Park. The NC Natural Heritage Progam lists portions of this site as 7 out of 10 for natural diversity, which is exceptional for a suburban/urban location. Our first and second effort this year was incredibly effective and we look forward to the third one being the same. Our teams cut or pull the invasives and haul them out by the parking lot. Fuquay Varina Public Works loads all this into large trailers and hauls it away as they are filled. Last time, we filled two trailers, and there is plenty more to go! We suggest that folks wear long sleeved shirts and pants and bring gloves and water. Tools are provided, but feel free to bring any favorite personal tools as well. REGISTER HERE
Source: NC Wildlife Federation

item.title: The Imprint of Faith: Exhibition Opening at Zeitgeist Gallery & Bar — Fri Nov 20, 6:00 PM — Zeitgeist Gallery & Bar
item.description:
Zeitgeist Gallery & Bar is proud to present The Imprint of Faith: What Has Been Given, What Has Been Taken. Faith. Religion. Worship. Spirituality. Each has left an imprint on many of our lives, often by shaping our communities, our cultures, and even our mental health. For some, faith has given hope, peace, belonging, and resilience. For others, it has been twisted with trauma, shame, exclusion, or loss. Sometimes, it is both. As artists, we have the opportunity to explore and share these experiences through a multitude of mediums and ideas. Through art, we can examine the ways faith and spirituality have influenced our identities, relationships, and understanding of the world. During this holiday season, we aim to support thoughtful conversation through art. What has faith, religion or spirituality given you? What has it taken away? How has it changed the way you see yourself and the world around you?
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Ecotones: Transitional Zones Where Ecosystems Meet — Sat Nov 21, 10:00 AM — Bynum Mill Access at Lower Haw River State Natural Area
item.description:
Friends of Lower Haw is offering a program on ecotones, transitional areas of vegetation where different natural communities meet. Examples of ecotones include transitional areas between forest and meadow, or between riverbank and water body. Our guide will be naturalist and nature photographer Jason Brown. We’ll visit transition areas where birds and wildlife can be spotted. Our guide will also talk about how past land use and land management has had an influence on the flora and fauna occurring at the Lower Haw River State Natural Area. This event is free and open to the public. All ages are welcome.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: Trail Talks with TLC: Brumley South — Fri Dec 18, 9:00 AM — Brumley South- University Station Entrance
item.description:
Join TLC Executive Director, Sandy Sweitzer, for a walk at her favorite part of Brumley Nature Preserve. If you are a hiker or birder who has avoided Brumley South because of the mountain bikers, join us! You’ll discover dedicated walking trails with cool rock formations, beautiful hardwood forests, and just enough hills to make it fun – all without worrying about a biker whizzing past. Sandy will share the history of the preserve, this expansion, and plans for possible future expansions. item.title: Impact of Environment and Emissions on Food Systems — Tue Nov 17, 12:00 PM — Trent Drive Hall 040
item.description:
Food systems everywhere are affected by changes in climate and our environments. Studies have shown that CO2 emissions reduce nutritional density on core crops. Shifting weather patterns affect planting and harvest cycles, while flooding and drought destroy crops and significantly reduce agricultural yield. Microplastics are increasingly identified throughout our food supply.
This Think Global panel will highlight some of the unexpected ways that our food systems are being impacted by a changing world. Panelists will share how food sources have been affected within the communities where they work, addressing both agricultural and manufacturing conditions that influence how critical nutrition is delivered.

item.title: From Developmental Signals to Butterfly Wing Diversity — Tue Nov 17, 12:30 PM — Nanaline Duke 147
item.description:
My research group examines how developmental systems generate morphological diversity and the mechanisms underlying its evolution. We work with butterflies and moths, which provide a rich comparative system for testing how changes in genomic regulation and gene regulatory networks underlie the evolutionary diversification of traits such as wing color patterns and wing shapes. We aim to pinpoint the genetic and developmental mechanisms that organize the wing as an organ at multiple levels, from the establishment of positional information to the growth and remodeling that shape the wing, and the specification of cell identities that produce structural and pigmentary coloration. Finally, we connect these genetic and developmental mechanisms to ecological function by investigating how complex wing phenotypes contribute to defense and mate choice.
Source: Duke University

item.description: The Multi-Agent AI Playground is a hands-on walkthrough that introduces you to agentic AI-systems where AI models take actions, use tools, and work together to accomplish tasks. Through seven progressively complex examples, you'll build your understanding step by step, starting with the basics and working up to more advanced setups. You'll start with simple LLM debates, where AI models argue a topic while another acts as judge, then see how a single agent can use tools like a calculator or web search through the ReAct pattern (Reason → Act → Observe). From there, you'll see how multiple agents can collaborate by sharing information, how a "manager" agent can delegate work to specialized helpers (for example, to build, test, and review a game), and how agents can plan multi-step tasks on their own and even spawn new sub-agents to get the job done. item.title: Triangle Nuclear Theory Colloquium - Nuclear Physics with Dynamical Pions: A Neural Quantum State Approach — Tue Nov 17, 1:30 PM — None
item.description:
Neural Quantum States (NQS) have emerged as a promising approach to solving the nuclear many-body problem, offering flexible representations of strongly correlated wave functions. However, most existing applications treat nucleons as the only explicit degrees of freedom, with pion dynamics encoded in effective nuclear interactions.
In this talk, I will discuss our ongoing efforts to extend the NQS framework to systems containing both nucleons and dynamical pion fields. Working within a low-energy effective theory, we construct variational wave functions that describe nucleons coupled to quantized pion modes in a finite periodic volume. I will present preliminary results for one- and two-nucleon systems, illustrating the application of this framework to nuclear dynamics with explicit pionic degrees of freedom.
Source: Duke University
